title: A memory guard for focused experiments, and four months of trend
impact: Focused AOT A/B harnesses decide experiments now (251, 254, 258, 259, 260) and measured wall time only, so a candidate could halve latency and double memory unnoticed. `benchmark/shared/memory_probe.dart` closes that in the mode those harnesses must run in — chosen by elimination, since an AOT binary has no VM service (`Service.getInfo()` returns null, `--enable-vm-service` is rejected) and running under JIT to get one would change what exp 193 requires be measured under AOT. The load-bearing finding is which reading to gate on: on a lane crossing `sacrificeSlotThreshold`, sampled `currentRss` peak said +75% and `maxRss` said -1.7% about the same change. `maxRss` is the true high-water; a `currentRss` curve is a retention signal, and retention moves when reader isolates are sacrificed and hand pages back. Gate on `maxRss`, one process per lane. Validated: five runs per arm spread <=0.6 MB, inert control lanes identical across arms, and `--no-memory` moves wall time 1.3-2.4% (inside the floor). First use answers exp 260's unmeasured claim 260.4: peak RSS *falls* on every lane (-2.1% / -11.5% / -28.0%), refuting its arithmetic prediction that peak capacity could rise 22-25%. A sweep of eight checkpoints from v0.3.0 (which resolves, builds and runs the current harness unmodified) shows peak read-path memory FLAT within ~1 MB for three months across ~40 merged experiments including the whole transfer-shape arc, while wall time fell 25-40% — so no regression exists to fix, and the only movement is exps 259 and 260, both downward. Three findings for future runners: the guard is a tripwire for a doubling, not an instrument for 5% drift; seeding dominates the gated number (mixed6-10k sits at 89.5 MB before the measured reads, which add ~18 MB); and `select()` peaks at 95 MB reading a table holding ~1.5 MB, a ~60x ratio never decomposed.
